coverage_notes: Surface: trackers, agent backends/providers, GitHub features, Executor interface, Build Order and shipped skills. 52 features; lib_loc total (Elixir src/lib modules 134065; the rest is shipped skills, priv scripts and seed files) 212746 (Elixir modules measured with wc -l in the frozen snapshot, plus runtime scripts/skills that the snapshot copy omits, measured with git show 3339b88:<path> | wc -l and named in each feature's modules); test_loc total 137288; loc_saving_estimate total 90453 (lines deleted outright; for externalize, only deleted lines count, moved lines do not). Method: features_loc.py maps modules and test regexes per feature (scratch-integrations/features_loc.json lists each feature's modules and matched tests; no module is attributed twice). Usage sources: Config census: 68 config files (14 under ~/.aiur: config, config.archon and 12 backups; 54 repo-local: 40 aiur worktree copies, 8 other aiur side checkouts/backups, aiur-research, archon, kevinweaver-dev and 2 private; khala has no repo-local config and runs on ~/.aiur/config), which collapse to 16 distinct key/value sets, 2 of them private; parsed with scratch-integrations/cfgkeys.rb (key names only for private files). Executor commands from Claude transcripts (~/.claude/projects/-home-user-github-everdred-{aiur,archon,architecture-docs,khala,kevinweaver-dev,<private repo> (private) (private)}, window 2026-09-01..09-26, exec_cmds.py) and 436 Codex Executor sessions (cwd = repo root, 2026-07-17..09-16, codex_exec.py); agent tool calls from ~/.codex/sessions (tools.<name>( ) and Claude agent transcripts (mcp__aiur__*); retained run logs ~/.aiur/logs (39 dirs, 2026-09-15..09-26: telemetry.ndjson backend/remote fields, boot.out.log disabled_integrations, alerts.ndjson topics); 22 historical run-summary.json files (2026-08-08..09-21); daemon state ~/.config/aiur/*/*/ (decisions.ndjson, webhook_deliveries.ndjson, usage-ledger, metrics); ~/.aiur/repo/*/*/executor wake/event journals; ~/.aiur/model-usage.json, model-catalog.json, github-budget/budget.sqlite3 (sqlite3 -readonly); read-only gh api for webhook deliveries, rulesets, CODEOWNERS and label searches. Privacy: private repos appear only as key names and counts marked (private); no secret values were read into output (.env files were reduced to key names). Caveats: Claude transcripts only reach back to 2026-09-01 and run logs to 2026-09-15, so June-July usage (e.g. early Remote Control) is invisible; Codex tool-call counts include ~5% echo lines; dashboard page views are not logged (features 20, 45 usage is inferred). Overlaps flagged for the merge step: alert feed (integrations-38) and provider meters (15) overlap observability/dashboard; opencode (11) and Remote Control (09) overlap TUI; Build Order web (45) and GitHub cache page (20) overlap dashboard; message delivery (43) overlaps orchestrator; CLI handlers for Executor commands live in agent_control_cli.ex/cli.ex and are not counted here. Not covered here (belongs to other surfaces): usage accounting/price tables (src/lib/aiur/usage, usage_*), orchestrator lifecycle modules (ci_lifecycle, comment_wake, human_review, merged_ticket_reconciler) that consume GitHub events, `aiur init` GitHub setup (init/github.ex, init/github_app.ex, init/labels.ex), SSH worker hosts (worker.ssh_hosts: 0 configs, ssh.ex + workspace/remote.ex), session resume handles, and the dashboard HTTP observability API.

features.name: Tracker adapter boundary (Aiur.Tracker, TrackerIdentity)
features.description: Behaviour that routes tracker reads/writes to the configured adapter (github, linear, memory), plus versioned repository-qualified tracker identities and the tracker config schema.
features.usage_evidence: Every dispatch goes through it. tracker.kind is set in 16 of 16 distinct configs; all 66 public config files say github, the 2 private ones set tracker.kind (value not reported). No config anywhere sets any tracker.linear.* or tracker.memory key.
features.rationale: Needed as a seam for a test fake, but the multi-tracker identity versioning (tracker_identity.ex 291 lines) exists for a second real tracker that no run has ever configured.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep a thin port (list/claim/label/comment) with one production adapter (GitHub) and one in-memory fake. Drop identity versioning and per-kind branches in config inference (config.ex inferred_tracker_kind).

features.name: GitHub tracker adapter (issues, labels, state, comments, PRs, trust)
features.description: The GitHub implementation of the tracker: open-issue listing and snapshots, agent:* label state machine writes (IssueState.swap_labels), label bootstrap, comments, pull requests, human-review gate, dispatch authorization from issue timelines, bot identity and the single-account comment marker, GitHub-specific config (tracker.github.*), and the event-sourced open-ticket projection.
features.usage_evidence: The only tracker in production: 1,761 issues and 2,062 PRs across 6 repos (census). agent:* label events in the retained window: aiur 10,822, khala 2,267, archon 972. Hot files in the fix history: issues.ex 21 fix PRs, dispatch_authorization timeline cap chain #1454/#2535/#2749/#2816. tracker.github.identity_mode is set in 0 of 68 config files, so the single_account marker (agent_marker.ex) has never been active.
features.rationale: Core and used, but over-built: dispatch authorization paginates full issue timelines to re-derive who applied agent:todo (the source of the recurring 64 KiB/512 KiB/1 MiB truncation chain), label precedence healing races the agent writer, and github/config.ex is 1,090 lines.
features.rewrite_notes: One ticket-state authority that derives the desired agent:* label from labels + PR head + reviews/CI at head, applied by one writer (merged-fixes 5.2). Replace timeline pagination with a trusted-actor check on the label event (webhook or events feed) or a cached per-issue fingerprint. Drop identity_mode=single_account and agent_marker.ex. Fold github/config.ex into the config schema.

features.name: Linear tracker (+ linear_graphql agent tool, Codex linear skill)
features.description: Linear GraphQL client and tracker adapter, the linear_graphql dynamic tool offered to every agent, the tracker.linear.* config keys, init wizard questions, and the Codex-native linear skill (.codex/skills/linear, 388 lines, not counted in lib_loc).
features.usage_evidence: No config in 68 files (16 distinct, 2 private) sets tracker.linear.* or a legacy linear: section. Boot logs: the 30 retained boots that log disabled_integrations all say "Linear tracker off (no LINEAR_API_KEY)" (rg disabled_integrations ~/.aiur/logs). LINEAR_API_KEY is absent from ~/.aiur/.env and every repo .env (key names only). The linear_graphql tool was called 14 times by Codex agents, all in GitHub-tracked workspaces (rg tools.linear_graphql( ~/.codex/sessions), i.e. misfires. The Codex linear skill was read 3 times.
features.rationale: Unused since the June 2 import (11 commits), yet it is offered as a tool to every agent turn, adds a second tracker shape to config/identity/init, and costs ~160 references outside linear/.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete linear/, codex/dynamic_tool/linear_graphql.ex, the tracker.linear schema, init questions, env schema entry, and the linear Codex skill. Test lines estimated (~300 inside extensions_test.exs and workspace_and_config_test.exs plus linear_graphql_test.exs 113).

features.name: Memory tracker
features.description: In-process tracker adapter (tracker.kind: memory) used as a test double.
features.usage_evidence: tracker.kind memory appears in 0 of 68 configs. It is referenced from 26 test files (110 references: rg Memory.Tracker / kind "memory" in src/test), so it is a test fixture shipped in the production library.
features.rationale: Earns its keep as a fake, but it belongs in test support, not in the shipped tracker kinds and config inference.
features.rewrite_notes: Move to test/support as the in-memory implementation of the tracker port; remove memory from tracker.kind validation and inferred_tracker_kind.

features.name: Backend registry and routing (agent.priority, agent.routing, model:/complexity: labels)
features.description: Single registry of coding-agent backends (codex, claude, claude-repl, kimi, deepseek, openrouter, test fake) with capabilities, presentation, pricing dimensions and account-generation metadata; route grammar backend[:model[:effort]][+remote]; per-ticket model:<backend>/model:<effort> label overrides; complexity routing table; deprecated agent.kind / switch_model_on_ratelimit / rate_limit_primary / rate_limit_fallback resolution.
features.usage_evidence: agent.priority set in 7 of 16 distinct configs (1 private); agent.routing.1-5 in 10 of 16 (2 private); agent.kind in 11 of 16. Per-backend sections are written three ways: agent.deepseek.enabled (9 distinct configs), root-level sections, agent.backend_configs.* (0 configs). Labels currently on issues (GitHub search, read-only): aiur model:codex 154, model:claude 115, model:deepseek 28, model:remote 1; khala model:codex 31, model:claude 23.
features.rationale: Needed: every dispatch resolves a route. Over-built: three spellings of per-backend config, four deprecated keys still resolved, UI presentation colours and pricing dimensions live in the backend registry (coding_agent.ex is 1,392 lines).
features.rewrite_notes: One route list (agent.priority) plus an optional complexity table. One per-backend section path. Remove deprecated keys with a load-time error. Move presentation to the UI package and pricing to the usage package.

features.name: Shared app-server adapter layer
features.description: Common JSON-RPC-over-stdio run skeleton for app-server backends (Codex app-server and the aiur-claude adapter): RPC framing, turn loop and state, interrupts, operator delivery at safe checkpoints, provider turn ledger, dynamic-tool call ledger (DETS) and oversized tool-result spill.
features.usage_evidence: Every Codex and headless Claude turn uses it: census 1,188 Codex + 1,278 Claude top-level agent sessions; telemetry lifecycle records with backend=codex 2,213 and backend=claude 1,271 (rg "backend":"..." over 39 retained telemetry.ndjson files).
features.rationale: Core shared transport; it is the reason two backends cost less than two full adapters.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep as the backend SDK boundary. It is the natural package seam for backend plugins (codex, claude, openai-compat).

features.name: Codex app-server backend
features.description: Codex adapter over `codex app-server`: handshake/thread resume, approvals and sandbox policy, notification routing, event normalization and humanizing, transcript extraction, user-input auto-answers, session recovery.
features.usage_evidence: Census: 6,000 Codex agent sessions (1,188 top-level + 4,812 subagent threads) 2026-07-16 to 09-26; 2,213 backend=codex lifecycle records in retained telemetry; run summaries 2026-08-08..09-02 show codex in 12 of 14 aiur runs. agent.codex.command/approval_policy set in 15 of 16 distinct configs; turn_sandbox_policy in 5.
features.rationale: Primary backend by volume; its fixes (transport EPIPE, queued-turn recovery) held after July.
features.rewrite_notes: Package as a backend plugin on the app-server SDK. event_humanizer.ex (510) is presentation and can move to the UI package.

features.name: Claude headless backend (via sibling aiur-claude app-server)
features.description: Claude adapter that drives the external `aiur-claude` Node app-server (sibling repo aiur-team/aiur-claude) through the shared app-server protocol; config, transcript extraction, event humanizing.
features.usage_evidence: Census: 1,278 Claude top-level agent sessions + 375 subagent transcripts; most of archon (332 vs 36 Codex) and khala (722 vs 128). 1,271 backend=claude lifecycle records in retained telemetry; 5,750 claude.app_server.turn_completion usage-ledger records across state dirs. agent.claude.command set in 11 of 16 distinct configs. The global config (khala) routes every complexity to claude.
features.rationale: Second production backend and the dominant one in September.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep as a backend plugin. The aiur-claude sibling is already externalized; keep the protocol contract (incl. provider_error marker) versioned between the two repos.

features.name: Claude REPL transport and Remote Control (claude-repl, model:remote, +remote)
features.description: Persistent interactive `claude` REPL in a tmux pane (launcher, prompt submit, operator inject, transcript-tail and hook-driven turn loops, reaper), Claude Code lifecycle hooks posted to /api/v1/:id/claude-hook, RC attach/URL harvest, display tailer, and live promotion/demotion of a running agent into remote-control mode.
features.usage_evidence: Dispatch telemetry carries a remote flag: 3,311 retained records (09-15..09-26) are all "remote":false, and 817 "remote": false and 0 "remote": true records appear in the 22 run-summary.json files (08-08..09-21). No retained telemetry or log line names backend claude-repl (rg claude-repl ~/.aiur/logs = 0). GitHub labels now: model:remote on 1 aiur issue, model:claude-repl on 0 in aiur/archon/khala. agent.remote_control is set in 0 of 68 configs. The code was last substantively extended in July (repl_agent.ex 32 commits 06-08..07-15).
features.rationale: No observed dispatch in two months, yet it forces --no-dashboard rejection rules, a remote branch in dispatch, and RC checks in ~20 other modules (pause_containment, process_reaper, shutdown, status_report, agent_teardown, rate_limit_fallback ...).
features.rewrite_notes: Delete claude/repl*, remote_control, display/transcript tailers, hook endpoint and settings, RemoteControlMode, the +remote route suffix and model:remote alias, and the RC branches elsewhere (~300 lines estimated). If interactive Claude is wanted later, run it as a separate backend plugin.

features.name: OpenAI-compatible backends (DeepSeek, Kimi/Moonshot, OpenRouter)
features.description: Direct OpenAI-compatible coding-agent adapter with its own tool loop (command runner, bounded glob, tool specs/parsing, conversation/checkpoint), a provider registry (kimi, deepseek, openrouter with base URLs, key env names, quirks), OpenRouter provider routing, per-provider usage adapters, and peak-pricing avoidance (agent.pricing_policy, price window).
features.usage_evidence: DeepSeek: backend=deepseek appears in 5 aiur run summaries 2026-08-16..09-01 (868 records; rg '"backend": "deepseek"'), 1,133 deepseek.openai_compat.request_usage usage-ledger records, 28 aiur issues still labelled model:deepseek, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY present in ~/.aiur/.env (name only), model-catalog.json last fetched deepseek 2026-09-03. deepseek is in agent.priority of 4 distinct configs (49 files, mostly August aiur worktree copies) and agent.deepseek.enabled is true in 9, but none of the configs that ran in September routes to it (aiur priority claude,codex; khala routes claude; archon claude). Kimi and OpenRouter: 0 labels, 0 ledger rows, 0 run-summary rows, no MOONSHOT_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY in any .env, no catalog entry.
features.rationale: A third, self-contained agent runtime (its own tool loop and sandboxing) that was used for two weeks in August and not since; Kimi and OpenRouter specifics were never exercised. It fits a backend plugin on the app-server/adapter SDK, not the core.
features.rewrite_notes: Move the generic OpenAI-compatible adapter to an optional backend package; delete the kimi and openrouter registry entries, OpenRouter provider-routing keys, per-provider usage adapters and the peak-pricing window (~800 deleted, rest moved).

features.name: opencode chat-pane bridge (TUI agent chat viewer)
features.description: Runs `opencode serve` + `opencode attach` panes per slot, injects each agent transcript into opencode's private SQLite schema (pinned row shapes), serves a synthetic /v1/chat/completions bridge so opencode can "chat" with an agent, pre-warms sessions, manages slot/attach pools and a custom theme. It is a viewer, not an agent backend.
features.usage_evidence: Only the three retained runs with debug logs have aiur.log: each shows opencode_bridge starting and no slot/serve/attach line (rg opencode ~/.aiur/logs/*/log/aiur.log). No chat-pane recordings exist (find ~/.aiur/logs -name "*.ansi" = 0). Executors launch headless: --bg in 136 transcript commands (Claude 9, Codex 127). opencode.* keys set in 4 of 16 distinct configs; pre_warmed_sessions defaults to 3 (archon sets 0). opencode.db holds no Aiur-injected agent sessions now (sessions are GC'd, so history is unknown). 48 commits since June.
features.rationale: One of the largest blocks in this surface (45 modules, 9k lines) couples Aiur to a third-party app's private SQLite schema and CLI, for a pane the operating mode (headless + dashboard/CLI) does not use.
features.rewrite_notes: Replace with a plain transcript tail (logs/agent.md) in the TUI chat pane, or move the whole TUI to its own package. Delete bridge, slots, attach pool, session writer, SQLite injection and theme. Coordinate with the TUI surface inventory.

features.name: Agent dynamic tools (emit_event, emit_alert, blockers, subscriptions, review threads, set_ticket_state)
features.description: Client-side tools Aiur offers every agent turn (Codex dynamic tools; exposed to Claude agents as mcp__aiur__* by aiur-claude): emit_event, emit_alert, aiur_declare_blocker/aiur_unblock, aiur_subscribe/aiur_unsubscribe, aiur_reply_review_thread/aiur_resolve_review_thread, aiur_set_ticket_state, with a 430-line error catalog.
features.usage_evidence: Calls counted in agent transcripts (Codex: rg "tools.<name>(" ~/.codex/sessions, ~5% are echo lines; Claude: tool_use names in ~/.claude/projects/*aiur-workspaces*): emit_event 6,495 + 1,992; emit_alert 3,874 + 988; aiur_set_ticket_state 0 + 296 (added #2808); aiur_declare_blocker 233 + 23; aiur_unblock 34 + 1; aiur_subscribe 2 + 1; aiur_unsubscribe 0 + 0; aiur_reply_review_thread 0 + 0; aiur_resolve_review_thread 0 + 0.
features.rationale: The event/alert/blocker/ticket-state tools are the agent half of the control plane and heavily used; the review-thread and subscribe tools are dead weight in every turn's tool list.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep emit_event, emit_alert, declare_blocker/unblock, set_ticket_state. Cut review-thread reply/resolve and subscribe/unsubscribe tools (agents are auto-subscribed). Shrink errors.ex to typed error codes.

features.name: Provider rate/usage-limit detection, pause and fallback reroute
features.description: Per-adapter refusal detection (Codex usageLimitExceeded/rateLimits and reset parsing, Claude session-limit banner/provider_error and IANA reset parsing), durable ModelAvailability observations in model-usage.json with backoff streaks, automatic reroute of a running agent to the next eligible route, and route-failure / missing-credential classification.
features.usage_evidence: ~/.aiur/model-usage.json is live (claude limited with reset 2026-09-26T08:40Z; codex limit_streak 15; 14 repo-local copies exist). Wake streams: 41 ticket.agent.attention.codex-usage-limit and 32 paused-usage_limit_exhausted. Retained alerts: 8 ticket.agent.pause.fallback_started and 8 fallback_succeeded. Census: 71 khala and 20 aiur tickets ran on both backends. Fix history area I: 11 fix PRs, recurring (#2627 -> #2727 -> #2812/#2813, #2811/#2814 still open).
features.rationale: Needed (limits strand the fleet) but split across four signal sources and three owners, which is why it recurs.
features.rewrite_notes: One typed provider-refusal event {backend, kind, resets_at} emitted by each adapter, one recovery owner that holds the route and schedules resume (merged-fixes 5.4). Remove deprecated rate_limit_primary/fallback resolution.

features.name: Model catalog and provider model discovery
features.description: Asks codex/claude app-servers for model/list and OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Anthropic shape) for their catalogue, caches it in model-catalog.json (24 h TTL), rejects unsafe ids, records OpenRouter price drift.
features.usage_evidence: ~/.aiur/model-catalog.json holds claude (fetched 2026-09-25), codex (09-25) and deepseek (09-03) entries; no openrouter/kimi entry. agent.backend_configs.<b>.model_discovery is set in 0 of 68 configs.
features.rationale: model/list for the two CLIs is useful for validation; the provider-catalogue discovery, price-drift logging and id-rejection rules serve OpenRouter/Kimi, which never ran.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep app-server model/list for codex and claude (or a curated list). Move provider-catalogue sources with the OpenAI-compat plugin or delete them.

features.name: Provider meters and account generations
features.description: Background probes of provider quota/usage (Codex account/rateLimits, Claude usage API, OpenRouter credits, prepaid balance baselines), a projection/refresh scheduler, redacted snapshots for the dashboard Units page and `aiur usage`, and an account-generation registry (lifecycle, continuity, tombstones) that detects credential/account switches.
features.usage_evidence: `aiur usage` run 10 times in Executor transcripts (Claude 9, Codex 1). polling.usage_interval_seconds set in 0 configs. balance-baselines dirs exist in 9 state dirs. The Units page meters are the other consumer (dashboard surface).
features.rationale: 4.6k lines to show quota headroom; the account-generation machinery (opaque generations, tombstones, continuity) is the bulk and serves attribution precision nobody reads.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep one probe per backend returning {used, limit, resets_at} and store it next to model-usage.json; drop account generations and balance baselines. Merge with feature 13 state so limits and meters share one record.

features.name: Claude Code OTLP telemetry intake
features.description: Authenticated per-launch OTLP log receiver for Claude Code (claude_code.api_request events), with a pinned event contract, rate limits, replay buffer and a usage adapter that converts events into usage envelopes.
features.usage_evidence: It is armed for every claude/claude-repl launch (session_lifecycle.ex prepare_telemetry_launch), but nothing outside claude/telemetry* subscribes to its PubSub topics (rg claude_telemetry / subscribe_usage over src/lib), and 0 usage-ledger records carry source claude_code.api_request in any of 14 state dirs, while 5,750 Claude records come from claude.app_server.turn_completion.
features.rationale: A dead-end pipeline: it receives and validates events that no consumer reads.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete claude/telemetry*, the launch wiring and its supervision child. If per-request Claude cost is needed later, take it from aiur-claude turn completion (already recorded).

features.name: GitHub HTTP transport and client core
features.description: REST/GraphQL transport with bounded response collector, error taxonomy, endpoint classification, request origin tagging, durable request log, host-side gh wrapper, connectivity backoff/escalation, and the client facade.
features.usage_evidence: Every GitHub call. The broker keeps a rolling one-hour admissions ledger (sqlite3 -readonly ~/.aiur/github-budget/budget.sqlite3): 2,259 rows when sampled at about 15:42Z and 2,466 at 15:58Z on 2026-09-26. Wakes: 127 system.github.connectivity_lost. Fix history area H: 107 fix PRs; transport.ex 15, client.ex 13.
features.rationale: Core. The known defect is shape, not size: truncation is reported as an empty 200 (merged-fixes 2.7).
features.rewrite_notes: Return a typed :truncated from the bounded collector; one error classifier used by all callers (#2427).

features.name: GitHub budget broker and quota metering (github-cost, github-usage)
features.description: Host-wide admission broker (Python + SQLite, shared by the daemon and agent gh wrappers) with leases, per-actor hourly Core/GraphQL/search ceilings, local holds and broker-timeout signal; fleet quota view, GraphQL cost attribution per call site, quota/budget history for charts, credential headroom; budget-hold pauses; `aiur github-cost` and `aiur github-usage`.
features.usage_evidence: budget.sqlite3 rolling one-hour ledger: 2,466 admissions at 15:58Z on 2026-09-26 (1,520 billable, 946 non-billable such as 304s and /rate_limit), 10 policy rows. `aiur github-cost` 174 Executor invocations (Claude 91, Codex 83), `aiur github-usage` 20. Wakes: github-broker-unavailable 61, github-broker 36, github-budget-broker 28, github-budget-unwritable 19, github-budget 5. tracker.github.daemon_core_limit_per_hour set in 2 distinct configs, agent_core_limit_per_hour in 1. Fix chain 2.8 (#2010 -> #2468 "4th LocalHold site").
features.rationale: Needed: GitHub quota is the fleet's binding constraint. Over-built: three meter views (quota.ex 1,380, quota_usage, budget_map, budget_ledger, histories) and holds that every call site must handle.
features.rewrite_notes: Resolve holds inside the broker boundary (callers block or get a typed defer). One meter model feeding one CLI (merge github-cost and github-usage). Keep the SQLite broker; consider porting the Python broker into the daemon if agents reach it through a daemon socket.

features.name: GitHub read cache, ResourceStore and agent gh state cache
features.description: Restart-durable GitHub state keyed by resource identity (ResourceStore) with change events and a single fetch entry point, a transport-level read-through cache with per-resource TTL policy and metrics, write-through deposits from Aiur's own mutations, the agent-side gh answer cache and its bridge/metrics, cache history, and view-state demand/sweep.
features.usage_evidence: On every read path. ~/.aiur/github-budget/state-cache holds 3,875 agent-cache files; github_resources.json exists in 10 state dirs. resource_store.ex: 22 of 23 PRs touching it were fixes (96%). Open issues #2413 (three caches, none reads the others) and #2245 (pollers bypass ResourceStore); read-cache hit rate regressed 9.0% -> 0.0% once (#2372).
features.rationale: Three overlapping caches (ResourceStore, ReadCache, agent gh cache) duplicate one concept; freshness is a per-caller flag, which caused the blocked_by regression chain (merged-fixes 2.6, 2.9).
features.rewrite_notes: Merge into one store that owns freshness (versioned deposits invalidated by webhook/poll events) and serves both the daemon and agent gh wrappers through one read path.

features.name: GitHub cache inspector page (/github-cache)
features.description: Dashboard debug page with a read-only projection of the GitHub state cache, redaction, cache/quota charts and budget map.
features.usage_evidence: 225 mentions of github-cache/github_cache in Executor transcripts since 09-01, mostly while developing the cache (#2073 work); no page-view log exists, so direct operator use is unknown. github_cache_live.ex had 15 commits 08-17..08-24 and none after.
features.rationale: A development aid for the cache work; once feature 19 is one store, `aiur github-cost`/status can show the few numbers that matter.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete the LiveView, charts/styles and CacheInspector; expose cache hit/miss counters in status JSON.

features.name: GitHub App auth, auth preflight and tracker health
features.description: GitHub App installation-token minting/refresh with least-privilege verification (daemon writes as <app>[bot]), authentication preflight diagnostics, and tracker/connectivity health state.
features.usage_evidence: Boot logs: GitHub App auth on in 8 and off ("using the GITHUB_TOKEN fallback") in 22 of the 30 retained boots that log it; the 8 are aiur runs 09-15..09-17, the 22 include every khala run. tracker.github.github_app.account set in 11 of 16 distinct configs (0 private). Census: aiur-daemon[bot] applied 2,099 agent:* label events in aiur and 359 in archon. GITHUB_APP_* names are absent from every .env; a key file exists under ~/.aiur/.keys. Alerts: 4 system.github_app_token.identity_mismatch, 12 system.tracker.auth_preflight_failed wakes.
features.rationale: Gives the daemon an identity separate from the agents, which the review/merge separation depends on; preflight turns silent 401/403s into named failures.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep; fold tracker_health connectivity state into the transport (feature 17).

features.name: GitHub credential pooling (tracker.github.credentials)
features.description: Registry and selector that spread daemon read traffic across several GitHub credentials (app_installation, machine_user, human) with per-credential write permission and enable flags.
features.usage_evidence: tracker.github.credentials (and every sub-key) is set in 0 of 68 config files (0 of 16 distinct, incl. private). Added 08-20..08-22 (5 commits), unchanged since.
features.rationale: Unused multi-credential routing on the hottest code path.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete registry/selector and the schema; keep a single credential resolution (GITHUB_TOKEN or App).

features.name: Agent gh/git guard (quota guard wrapper, push guard, token scrub)
features.description: Installs wrappers so every gh/git an agent runs goes through the budget broker and replay cache, injects the credential from a file only for governed calls (agents never inherit GITHUB_TOKEN), and guards pushes.
features.usage_evidence: Every agent gh/git call: per-repo github-quota/agent-processes.tsv and daemon-requests.tsv in 3 state dirs; broker admissions attribute agent consumers. Wakes: github-permissions 71, github-write-access 69, workflow-permissions 69 (khala), github-credential* 4. Fix chain "agent credentials" #2270..#2728, #2667 open.
features.rationale: Needed for quota and credential isolation, but it is a 3.4k-line bash re-implementation of policy that the daemon also implements (5.8k lines of tests guard it).
features.rewrite_notes: Keep a thin shim that forwards gh/git to one broker/cache (daemon socket or the Python broker) and injects the token; move classification and caching logic out of bash.

features.name: GitHub polling loops (dispatch poll, comments, CI, firehose, ls-remote, cadence)
features.description: The poll drivers that turn GitHub state into events: open-issue/label dispatch poll, comment/review poller with GraphQL batch PR discovery, CI poller for in-flight PR heads, repo-events firehose, ls-remote branch ticker with branch-ref store, ready-for-review transitions, poll cadence classes and idle widening.
features.usage_evidence: Wake records by family across 9,760 records: ticket.branch 1,789, ticket.pr 1,287, ticket.ci 862 (ticket.ci.passed 619, failed 247). polling.interval_seconds set in 16 of 16 distinct configs (values 30 and 120 in public ones); polling.intervals in 2 (1 private). Fix history: github_comments_poller.ex 21 fix PRs (88% fix share); idle backoff chain #2025 -> #2818 open.
features.rationale: The default event source and heavily used; the per-class cadence knobs and the idle-backoff interactions are where latency bugs recur.
features.rewrite_notes: One poll scheduler reading through the unified store (feature 19), a single cadence with demand-triggered refresh, no per-class knobs that the docs themselves call dead (firehose, ci).

features.name: GitHub webhooks (ingress, delivery log, delivery modes, deposit/normalizer)
features.description: HMAC-verified /api/v1/github/webhook receiver, idempotent delivery log (72 h), per-repo delivery-mode state machine (polling vs proven webhook) with silence sweep and widened polling, and a deposit/normalizer that writes webhook bodies into the store and publishes the same events as the pollers.
features.usage_evidence: GitHub side (read-only gh api): only aiur-team/aiur has a hook (khala and archon, the September fleets, have none); all 3,524 deliveries GitHub still retains (2026-09-24..09-26) failed, last_response 502. Aiur side: the only non-empty webhook_deliveries.ndjson accepted 5,721 deliveries on 2026-08-12..08-15; every later state dir (aiur, khala, archon, architecture-docs, private) has 0. webhooks.repos set in 3 of 16 distinct configs; AIUR_GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET present in ~/.aiur/.env (name only). No webhook alert or wake topic appears in any retained log.
features.rationale: Polling is the complete, default event source; the webhook path duplicates it (equivalence tests exist to keep the two identical) and has been failing unnoticed for the whole retained window.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete ingress, delivery log, delivery modes, deposit and normalizer. If quota later requires push delivery, add it behind the unified store as one more event source, measured per AGENTS.md "A claimed saving must be measured".

features.name: CI readiness, merge-queue detection and CI approval ledger
features.description: Checks whether a repo can merge Aiur PRs (required checks produced by workflows, token scope), classifies PRs parked outside a merge queue, records per-PR CI approvals/draft state, and the human-only-merge ruleset scripts.
features.usage_evidence: Retained alerts: system.ci_readiness.not_ready 1,050 and unavailable 8 (rg over *alerts.ndjson in ~/.aiur/logs and ~/.config/aiur). Two stored assessments (~/.aiur/ci-readiness.json for architecture-docs 09-03 ready; aiur .aiur/ci-readiness.json 08-18 not ready). AIUR_CI_READINESS_TOKEN present in ~/.aiur/.env. Rulesets (gh api read-only): human-only-merge-gate active on aiur-team/aiur only. ci-approvals.json in 2 state dirs.
features.rationale: The check is useful at init and on demand; as a running monitor it produced 1,050 not_ready alerts, which is noise.
features.rewrite_notes: Run readiness in `aiur init`/`status` only; keep the CI approval ledger inside the ticket-state authority; drop the separate operator-only token if the App token has workflow scope.

features.name: Review threads (read, reply, resolve, resolution policy)
features.description: Reads PR review threads, supports reply/resolve mutations, a pure resolution policy, and thread identity for comment events.
features.usage_evidence: Read side feeds comment wakes and the pr_health thread-clearance gate (rework_requeue_failed path). Mutation side: agents called aiur_reply_review_thread 0 times and aiur_resolve_review_thread 0 times (Codex and Claude transcripts).
features.rationale: Reads are needed; the mutation half has no caller in practice.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep thread reads; delete reply/resolution/resolution_policy and the two agent tools (agents use gh directly when they must).

features.name: GitHub native issue dependencies (blocked_by) and blocker subscriptions
features.description: Issue Dependencies REST API reads/writes, declare/remove dependency domain, relationships, the bounded blocked_by read used by the dispatch gate, and automatic blocker/blockee event subscriptions.
features.usage_evidence: Agents declared 256 blockers (233 Codex + 23 Claude) and unblocked 35 times; Build Order graphs are built from these edges (11 labelled roots). Fix chain 2.6 (#1821 -> #2720, incl. the #2714 budget incident).
features.rationale: Needed for dependency gating and Build Order.
features.rewrite_notes: Serve blocked_by from the unified store with store-owned freshness (no per-caller revalidate flag).

features.name: CODEOWNERS author allowlist
features.description: Parses CODEOWNERS to decide whose comments are trusted directions to agents, refreshes it on a cadence, and edits CODEOWNERS from `aiur init`.
features.usage_evidence: Consulted by the event sanitizer for every comment event. .github/CODEOWNERS exists in aiur-team/aiur and aiur-team/khala, not in archon (gh api read-only). events.codeowners_refresh_seconds set in 0 configs. Four overlapping allowlists exist: CODEOWNERS, tracker.github.trusted_accounts (6 of 16 distinct configs), allowed_users (6), human_mergers (11, 1 private).
features.rationale: Four trust lists answer the same question (who may direct or merge); CODEOWNERS parsing plus editing is 1.3k lines for it.
features.rewrite_notes: Merge into one trust policy: trusted_accounts (direct agents) and human_mergers (merge), optionally seeded from CODEOWNERS at init; drop the runtime parser/refresh and the init editor.

features.name: PR health scan and rework re-queue
features.description: Periodic scan of open PRs raising unmergeable-author, stale-unreviewed and rework-merge-only alerts, and moving a reworked PR back to human-review when its own diff changed since CHANGES_REQUESTED.
features.usage_evidence: pr_health.enabled true in 2 of 16 distinct configs (aiur and aiur-research). Retained alerts: system.pr_health.stale_unreviewed 82, unmergeable_author 54, rework_requeue_failed 0.
features.rationale: The alerts are cheap and useful; the re-queue is one of five writers that decide rework state (merged-fixes 2.2).
features.rewrite_notes: Move the re-queue rule into the single ticket-state authority (feature 02 notes); keep the scan as three alert checks.

features.name: PR watch and /aiur PR comment commands
features.description: Opt-in watching of human PRs via a watch label, repo-wide scan for one-off /aiur or @bot PR comment commands, and PR-anchored routing/teardown of agents working on human PRs.
features.usage_evidence: pr_watch.* is set in 0 of 68 configs (default enabled: false), so command_scan, pr_anchored and target selection branches never run. Executor transcripts show 24 lines mentioning /aiur watch|merge|rework or agent:watch, none enabling it.
features.rationale: Default-off feature with no config enabling it anywhere.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete command_scan, pr_anchored, pr_command_scanner, the pr_watch schema and the gated branch in comment_polling/target_selection (~80 lines).

features.name: Agent event bus (topics, subscriptions, publisher, sanitizer)
features.description: AMQP-style topic exchange for cross-ticket events, per-issue persistent subscription stores, universal agent subscriptions, restart-safe event ids, shared publisher, six-layer sanitizer and external-content wrapping for GitHub text, publication audit log.
features.usage_evidence: Carries every wake (9,760 wake records) and every agent-visible GitHub event; 126 per-ticket subscriptions.json files in retained logs; agents emitted 8,487 custom events (emit_event). Explicit subscribe calls: 3.
features.rationale: The core event pipe between GitHub, agents and the Executor.
features.rewrite_notes: Simplify topic patterns to the few classes in use (ticket.<id>.{pr,ci,branch,agent,comment}, system.*) if the rewrite drops custom subscriptions.

features.name: Executor wake inbox and executor-wait (claims, roster, principal)
features.description: Durable identifier-only wake ledger per repo (<repo>.executor.wakes.ndjson + cursor + pending), bounded to 10,000 records; executor-wait long-poll with auto-claim; a leased single-owner claim with TTL, roster states (active/idle/stalled/expired) and principal registration for --executor runs; recovery commands.
features.usage_evidence: Wake records: aiur 4,749, architecture-docs 1,881, archon 810, khala 2,203, <private repo> (private) (private) 117 (census). Executor commands (Claude transcripts since 09-01 + Codex Executor sessions): executor-wait 31 + 795, executor-roster 10 + 26, executor-revoke 0 + 7, executor-release 1 + 0, executor-fast-forward 1 + 0, executor-claim 0 + 0, --executor 0 + 1. Executors also read the file directly (commands naming *.executor.wakes.ndjson, mostly tail -F: 254 + 72) and the khala Executor wrote its own wake-relay.py and native-wake-relay.py in its state dir.
features.rationale: The inbox and wait are the Executor's main input and are used; the multi-consumer lease/roster/revoke/fast-forward machinery is barely used, and Executors still build relays around it.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep the ledger + cursor + a blocking wait that also pushes (one stream the Executor can follow natively). Replace claims/roster/principal with a single-owner lock and a staleness check.

features.name: Executor event journal, listener and custom executor.* events (listen/emit/subscribe)
features.description: Supervised daemon listener that reduces allowlisted events to wakes, a durable Executor event journal with cursor, and CLI commands to stream events, publish custom executor.* events and manage persistent Executor bindings.
features.usage_evidence: The journal is used only for decisions: 266 records across aiur/architecture-docs/archon/khala, of which 265 are executor.decision.requested/deferred and 1 is a custom executor.khala.monitor_check. Commands: executor-listen 0 + 11, executor-emit 0 + 4, executor-subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions 0 + 0 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts).
features.rationale: The listener that feeds the wake inbox is needed; the Executor-facing pub/sub surface is not used.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep the listener as an internal wake producer. Cut executor-listen, executor-emit, executor-subscribe/unsubscribe/subscriptions and custom executor.* topics (CLI handlers counted with the CLI surface).

features.name: Decision/Command store, delivery and Executor answer CLI
features.description: Durable event-sourced Decisions ("Commands") raised by agents: validation, provenance, attention classification, blocking gate, expiry, answer recording, delivery to whichever worker runs the ticket, dispatch tasks, dismissal/moot/escalation, history and query/projection; `aiur commands`, `aiur executor-answer|escalate|moot`.
features.usage_evidence: decisions.ndjson across 14 state dirs (~/.config/aiur/*/*): 595 requested, 81 answer_recorded, 285 decision_expired, 514 failed (delivery), 38 decision_mooted, 22 executor_escalated, 52 delivered, 45 consumed. Only ~14% of requests got an answer. Commands used: `aiur commands` 130 + 66, executor-answer 39 + 12, executor-escalate 23 + 12, executor-moot 9 + 2 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). Wakes: 143 ticket.agent.attention.operator-decision. Fix history area M: 17 fix PRs; decision_store.ex is the largest file in my surface (4,826 lines).
features.rationale: Agents do need a way to ask and be answered, but 13k lines deliver an answer in 14% of cases and fail delivery more often than they succeed.
features.rewrite_notes: A small ask/answer record keyed to the ticket: {question, options, blocking, answer, delivered_at}, answered by CLI or dashboard, delivered at the next turn via the agent queue. Drop attention classification variants, dispatch tasks, retained-index snapshots and legacy pagination.

features.name: Decision revisions, enrichment and decision latency metrics
features.description: Revision requests and their dispatch, supervisor enrichment of a decision, and a decision-latency metrics writer/collector (metrics/decision_latency.ndjson) feeding a dashboard latency panel.
features.usage_evidence: Across ~1,800 decision events in 14 state dirs there is no revision or enrichment event type (event types seen: requested, failed, decision_expired, answer_recorded, dispatch_queued, delivered, consumed, acknowledged, resolved, deferred, escalated, mooted, dismissed, dispatch_outcome_unknown, handed_off), and all 595 requested decisions carry revision_sequence 0 (rg revision_sequence), so no revision or `executor-answer --supersede` replacement was ever accepted. The metrics writer does run (decision_latency.ndjson: khala 607, aiur 706+85, kevinweaver-dev 382 lines) but its only reader is a dashboard panel.
features.rationale: Unexercised workflow branches plus a metrics pipeline for a panel.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete revisions (this also removes `executor-answer --supersede`, which is the revision path), enrichment and decision_metrics; compute answer latency on read from the decision record if a panel needs it.

features.name: Supervisor Decision HTTP API (bearer token)
features.description: Machine-facing /api/v1/decisions read/decide endpoints for a supervising Executor authenticated by AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN, with fail-closed delegation/authority policy (decisions.supervisor_allowed_kinds).
features.usage_evidence: All 30 retained boots that log disabled_integrations report "Supervisor Decision API off (no AIUR_SUPERVISOR_TOKEN)". decisions.supervisor_allowed_kinds / supervisor_allow_non_reversible are set in 0 of 68 configs. Executors answered through the CLI (executor-answer) instead; 6 /api/v1/decisions mentions in aiur Executor transcripts and 1 decide call in architecture-docs.
features.rationale: A parallel answer path that is never enabled; the CLI covers it.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete DecisionApi, its controller, supervisor auth/token, delegation/authority policy and the decisions config section. A future remote Executor can use the same RPC as the CLI.

features.name: Alert feed and ledger (aiur alerts, needs-attention)
features.description: Project-scoped durable alert ledger, structured alert emission (with optional sounds), alert topics and the feed read by `aiur alerts` and the watch actionable section.
features.usage_evidence: `aiur alerts` 143 + 459 invocations (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). 37% of aiur wakes are needs_attention (census). alerts.enabled set in 11 of 16 distinct configs (sound switch). Fix history area J: 44 fix PRs; false/re-raised alert chain 2.15 still open (#2811, #2819).
features.rationale: The Executor's primary attention signal. Its problem is lifecycle (conditions not keyed), not size.
features.rewrite_notes: Key each alert to a condition with an owner and a resolve rule; move sounds (alerts.use_os_default_sounds, sound_dir, alerts_file) to the TUI/Stream Deck package. Overlaps the observability surface inventory.

features.name: Asks (aiur ask / aiur asks)
features.description: Append-only Executor-authored requests to the human operator, listed by `aiur asks` and printed by status when blocking.
features.usage_evidence: meta/asks.ndjson: 5 records ever, all in aiur (0 in archon, khala, architecture-docs, private). Commands: ask 0 + 9, asks 3 + 5 (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts).
features.rationale: Same shape as a blocking Command (question for a human); a second store for it is redundant.
features.rewrite_notes: Represent an ask as a Decision raised by the Executor principal; delete asks store and CLI.

features.name: Findings ledger (aiur findings)
features.description: Host-local NDJSON ledger of Executor findings with record/unfiled/slugs/digest views, used by /aiur-meta.
features.usage_evidence: meta/findings.ndjson: aiur 43, khala 13, kevinweaver-dev 9, archon 8 records. `aiur findings` 17 + 108 invocations.
features.rationale: Small and used, but it is Executor tooling (aiur-meta), not daemon behaviour.
features.rewrite_notes: Move to the Executor skill package as a script over the same NDJSON file; no daemon RPC needed.

features.name: Executor takeover advisory alerts
features.description: Monitor that tracks each nonterminal ticket's convergence age and raises needs-attention takeover advisories at configurable thresholds.
features.usage_evidence: Retained alert logs: 46 system.executor_takeover.<n> and 6 .resolved. executor-takeover-alerts state dirs exist in 6 state dirs. executor_takeover_* keys set in 0 configs (defaults 8 h / 1 h).
features.rationale: 1k lines (monitor, snapshot, store) for one age threshold.
features.rewrite_notes: Compute convergence age in the status projection and raise one alert from the alert lifecycle; drop the separate monitor and store.

features.name: Executor handoffs
features.description: Seeds the machine-local executor/handoff.md per repository; the aiur-handoff skill writes and reads timestamped handoff documents.
features.usage_evidence: 86 handoff files: khala 61 (58 on 2026-09-18, median gap 4.4 min), aiur 18, archon 5, architecture-docs 2 (census). aiur-handoff Skill invocations: 3 (Claude Executor transcripts).
features.rationale: Tiny code; the value is in the skill. The khala burst is a skill/Executor behaviour problem, not a code one.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep in the Executor skill package; add a minimum interval or dedupe in the skill.

features.name: Executor-to-agent messages (aiur message)
features.description: Enqueues Executor text on an agent's native queue, delivers at a safe checkpoint or interrupts, auto-resumes paused entries, with message-id idempotency and delivered/queued/unknown outcomes.
features.usage_evidence: `aiur message` 53 + 275 invocations (Claude + Codex Executor transcripts). Fix chain: #1800 -> #2155 (enqueued reported as delivered).
features.rationale: The Executor's direct channel to agents.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep; share one delivery path with decision answers (feature 35). Modules overlap the orchestrator surface.

features.name: Build Order graph, catalog and CLI (daemon side)
features.description: Planning layer over GitHub issues: build-order root labels and sub-issue/blocked_by graphs, event-sourced catalog store, selected-root projection with cadence/policy, pack status on disk, ad-hoc source, ticket detail and history providers, progress rendering, `aiur build-orders`.
modules: src/priv/build_orders/*.json + README (2,515 lines of seed packs, in git 3339b88)
features.usage_evidence: GitHub search (read-only): 7 aiur, 3 archon, 1 khala issues carry the build-order root label. Pack dirs: aiur 6, architecture-docs 4, archon 2, khala 1 (+ private). `aiur build-orders` 32 + 36 Executor invocations; /build-orders referenced 72 times in Executor Claude transcripts. tracker.github.planning_* set in 5 of 16 distinct configs; build_order.* keys in 0. 56 commits 07-13..09-18.
features.rationale: Used a few times per repo, but it is a separate product (planning graph + views) that mostly reads GitHub; 11.5k lib + 8.6k web lines is the largest block in my surface.
features.rewrite_notes: Split into a Build Order package that reads the tracker store and publishes views; drop the event-sourced catalog cadences, ticket-history provider and selected-root policy layers (~4k deleted) in favour of on-demand graph reads.

features.name: Build Order dashboard pages
features.description: LiveView /build-orders catalog and root pages: graph, grid model, breakdown, selected root, ticket context drawer, usage/analytics scopes, presenters and data/planning sources.
features.usage_evidence: No page-view log exists. /build-orders appears in 72 Executor transcript commands (curl/screenshot checks, mostly during development). The Build Order cadence docs say a headless run with no page open buys no catalog reads.
features.rationale: Goes with the Build Order package (feature 44); overlaps the dashboard surface inventory.
features.rewrite_notes: Move with feature 44; collapse planning_source (926) / data_source / source_runtime / context_runtime layers into one view model (~2k deleted).

features.name: aiur-build planning skill (Build Order pack authoring and publication)
features.description: Executor skill that decomposes a feature into a validated planning pack and publishes it as GitHub issues with blocked_by edges; ships 14.5k lines of Python validators/publisher (3.4k of them tests) and 1k lines of markdown.
features.usage_evidence: Skill invocations: 2 in Claude Executor transcripts (archon, architecture-docs); SKILL.md read 20 + 9 times in Codex sessions. 13 pack dirs and 11 labelled roots exist (feature 44).
features.rationale: A standalone planning/publishing tool larger than most daemon subsystems; it only needs GitHub, not the daemon.
features.rewrite_notes: Move to its own skill/plugin repo; test_loc here is the Python tests inside the skill (not src/test).

features.name: Agent skill installer and bundled aiur agent skills (aiur-agent, aiur-debug, design-import)
features.description: Embeds skills at compile time and installs them into every ticket workspace under .claude/skills and .codex/skills (symlinks), plus the per-turn shared agent prompt that routes agents to aiur-agent.
features.usage_evidence: aiur-agent: 1,087 Skill invocations by Claude agents and ~8,500 SKILL.md reads in Codex sessions, 94% of which are agent sessions (exec/command lines only; the skill list injected into every session is excluded). aiur-debug: 0 Claude invocations, 35 Codex reads. design-import: 0 and 0.
features.rationale: The agent operating manual is read on essentially every ticket turn.
features.rewrite_notes: Keep aiur-agent and aiur-debug; drop design-import (0 reads) from the workspace set. Skill-text tests (aiur_agent_skill_test 842 lines) could shrink to link/structure checks.

features.name: Vendored Compound Engineering skills (31 skills, pinned 3.19.0)
features.description: The complete pinned Compound Engineering skill set vendored into .claude/skills (with .codex symlinks) and installed into every ticket workspace, refreshed by scripts/update-compound-engineering-skills.
features.usage_evidence: Reads in Codex sessions (exec/command lines; 94% agent sessions) + Claude agent Skill invocations: ce-code-review 3,363 + 103, ce-work 1,091 + 4, ce-plan 895, ce-doc-review 393, ce-simplify-code 355, ce-debug 349, ce-commit-push-pr 313, ce-resolve-pr-feedback 225 + 2, ce-commit 141 + 1, ce-brainstorm 85. Twenty skills have 0-3 agent reads: ce-babysit-pr, ce-compound, ce-compound-refresh, ce-dogfood, ce-explain, ce-handoff, ce-ideate, ce-optimize, ce-polish, ce-pov, ce-product-pulse, ce-promote, ce-proof, ce-riffrec-feedback-analysis, ce-setup, ce-strategy, ce-sweep, ce-test-browser, ce-test-xcode, lfg (25,506 lines).
features.rationale: Ten skills carry the agent workflow; the other twenty are vendored bulk that no agent reads.
features.rewrite_notes: Ship only the used subset into workspaces, or install the upstream plugin at a pinned version instead of vendoring; the Executor can still load the full plugin in its own session.

features.name: Codex-native git skills (commit, push, pull, land, linear)
features.description: Codex-only skills under .codex/skills for commit, push/PR, merge-based pull, land (with a 621-line land_watch.py) and raw Linear GraphQL.
features.usage_evidence: Codex exec reads: commit 119, push 89, pull 46, land 35, linear 3. skills.md also lists a `debug` Codex skill that does not exist at 3339b88.
features.rationale: Duplicates ce-commit / ce-commit-push-pr, which agents read more (141 and 313).
features.rewrite_notes: Merge commit/push into the CE commit skills; keep pull/land only if the merge policy needs them; delete linear (feature 03) and fix the stale debug entry in skills.md.

features.name: Executor skills (aiur-run, aiur-monitor, aiur-meta, aiur-intro, release)
features.description: Skills loaded by the Executor session: run operation end to end, monitoring, hourly meta audit, first contact/install, release. (aiur-build, aiur-handoff and aiur-debug are listed separately.)
features.usage_evidence: Claude Executor Skill invocations since 09-01: aiur-run 7, aiur-meta 1. SKILL.md reads across all Codex sessions (exec + older command format): aiur-run 161 + 129, aiur-monitor 40 + 10, aiur-meta 16, aiur-intro 8 + 6, release 0. /aiur-meta durable logs stopped after 2026-09-11 (census).
features.rationale: Executor procedure, not daemon code; they version with the operator, and tests in src/test assert their text.
features.rewrite_notes: Move to an Executor skill package with its own lint; cut aiur-run by ~1.5k lines of incident-specific rules (the file is 4.2k lines).

features.name: ElevenLabs provider (speech-to-text, TTS, quota meter)
features.description: Realtime STT sessions over Mint.WebSocket for Stream Deck/dashboard voice, streamed TTS replies, and an account-credit quota meter.
features.usage_evidence: ELEVENLABS_API_KEY present in ~/.aiur/.env and aiur/.env (names only). elevenlabs.* set in 0 of 68 configs (env fallback). No retained daemon log line names an ElevenLabs session; voice usage lives with the Stream Deck/dashboard surfaces, which I did not measure.
features.rationale: Only the voice surfaces use it; it belongs in the Stream Deck/voice package.
features.rewrite_notes: Move with the voice/Stream Deck package; the daemon keeps no provider credential for it.

features.name: rtk output-compression integration
features.description: Admission gate and savings reader for rtk, which rewrites agent shell output; refuses unless rtk excludes gh.
features.usage_evidence: agent.rtk.enabled set in 0 of 68 configs (default false).
features.rationale: Opt-in feature never enabled; the docs measure its saving as command-dependent.
features.rewrite_notes: Delete rtk.ex, the schema and the analytics panel hook.
